messages:
Mira Chen: quick question — saw an incident where client retries from the mobile SDK ended up routing a resident write to a different region, bypassing consent checks :thinking:
Sanjay Patel: ugh. is this the retry from the edge proxy or from the app client?
Mira Chen: looks like the mobile SDK retried after a 502 from proxyd, proxyd then sent it to the next healthy region (fallback pool). the request had X-Region: eu but proxyd drops it on retry.
Alex R.: do we have logs? can you paste the proxyd request/response trace?
Mira Chen: pasted core snippet from traces/logs:
```
REQUEST  -> proxyd-eu: POST /v1/tenant/123/generate
  headers: {"X-Region":"eu","Idempotency-Token":"tok-abc"}
proxyd -> upstream-eu returns 502 (overloaded)
client retry -> proxyd-us (next ip) forwards POST without X-Region header
upstream-us accepts and writes tenant 123 (residency: EU-only)
```
Sanjay Patel: ok that's solid reproduction. proxyd's retry path currently uses connection-level round robin and doesn't reattach region metadata.
Luca B.: this is dangerous for data residency. two quick approaches: (1) make proxyd sticky on initial region for retries, or (2) have proxyd reject retries that would violate residency with 409+hint. both have tradeoffs.
Jen K.: sticky is easiest but can increase tail latency if initial region is unhealthy. rejecting causes client complexity — SDK needs to surface to user and hunt for alternate flows.
Alex R.: what about using idempotency tokens + control-plane check before forwarding to a different region? proxyd could do a local lookup: if token seen/owner-region known -> route accordingly, else return 425 'needs-route' for client to re-resolve.
Mira Chen: love that. cheaper than full control-plane RPC if we keep a small token cache in proxyd. but cold tokens still a problem.
Sanjay Patel: we could also add an explicit header from client: `X-Region-Stick: prefer` and proxyd treats that as invariant for retries. default behavior remains optimistic.
Luca B.: note: compliance/legal requires we never *persist* EU-resident data in non-EU region. transient in-memory processing might be allowed but our policy is stricter. so proxyd must enforce hard blocks on cross-region commit.
Jen K.: ops perspective — implement proxyd guard that checks tenant residency flags before forwarding to a different region; if mismatch -> 402/409 with body {"action":"route-resolve"}. SDKs will map that to a re-resolve flow. low blast.
InfraBot: deploy check: proxyd v2.3 will add header-preserve-on-retry config + residency-guard feature-flag. rollout plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global. see deploy-id 98372.
Mira Chen: next steps I propose:
- short: add residency-guard reject on cross-region forward (feature-flagged)
- medium: implement idempotency-token cache lookup to route retries to original region
- long: make control-plane return routing hints to clients and SDKs so retries go to correct region instead of proxyd remapping
Sanjay Patel: agree. I'll draft a tiny RFC for proxyd retry semantics + token-cache. want to capture perf numbers for added lookups.
Alex R.: add test-case to our chaos harness: simulate 502 on primary region and ensure no resident write lands outside region.
Mira Chen: thanks all — I'll open the RFC + attach logs. ping me if you want in on design review :eyes:
